matrixOperations.dimensionErrorAdd: Matrices must have the same dimensions to be added
matrixOperations.dimensionErrorSubtract: Matrices must have the same dimensions to be subtracted
matrixOperations.sumRuleDescription: Matrix addition is performed by adding each corresponding element:
matrixOperations.subtractRuleDescription: Matrix subtraction is performed by subtracting each corresponding element:
matrixOperations.detailedCalculationsDescriptionAdd: We add each pair of corresponding elements:
matrixOperations.detailedCalculationsDescriptionSubtract: We subtract each pair of corresponding elements:
matrixOperations.dimensionErrorMultiply: The number of columns of the first matrix must equal the number of rows of the second
matrixOperations.multiplicationRuleDescription:
To calculate each element C_{i,j} of the result:

1. Take row i of A
2. Take column j of B
3. Multiply element-wise
4. Sum all products

Example: C_{1,1} = (row 1 of A) ⋅ (column 1 of B)
matrixOperations.detailedCalculationsDescriptionMultiply: We calculate each element step by step:
matrixOperations.transposeProcessDescription: 🔄 Each element of the original matrix moves according to the rule:
matrixOperations.determinantSquareError: The determinant can only be calculated for square matrices
matrixOperations.determinant1x1Description: For a 1×1 matrix, the determinant is simply the value of the single element.
matrixOperations.sarrusMethodDescription:
For 3×3 matrices, Sarrus' rule is more direct:
- Repeat the first two columns to the right
- Sum products of main diagonals
- Subtract products of secondary diagonals
matrixOperations.sarrusFinalDescription: Applying the full formula to obtain the determinant
matrixOperations.cofactors3x3MethodDescription: For a 3×3 matrix, we use the first row for expansion. Each element is multiplied by its corresponding cofactor. Cofactors alternate in sign: +, -, +.
matrixOperations.cofactors3x3FinalDescription: Multiply each element by its cofactor and sum.
matrixOperations.zerosMethodDescription:
We will look for the row or column with the most zeros or that allows creating more zeros easily.
We will use elementary operations to simplify the calculation.
matrixOperations.createZerosDescription:
We will use elementary operations to create zeros.
Remember: these operations do not change the determinant value (or multiply it by a known constant).
matrixOperations.pivotSelectedDescription:
Pivot: element [{{row}},{{col}}] = {{pivot}}
We will use this element to create zeros in the rest of the {{type}}.
matrixOperations.developByRowOrColumnDescription:
We now expand the determinant by the {{type}} {{index}}.
Thanks to the created zeros, many terms will be zero, simplifying the calculation.
matrixOperations.zeroElementDescription: This element is zero, so it does not contribute to the determinant.
matrixOperations.minorMatrixDescription:
{{size}}×{{size}} matrix obtained by removing row {{row}} and column {{col}}.
{{message}}
matrixOperations.determinant3x3Description:
We calculate the determinant of the 3×3 matrix using cofactor expansion.
Much simpler than calculating a 4×4 matrix directly!
matrixOperations.optimizedResultDescription:
Sum of all contributions from {{type}} {{index}}.
Thanks to the zero strategy, only non-zero terms are calculated.
matrixOperations.cofactorsMethodDescription:
We expand the matrix along the first row:
Each element a₁ⱼ is multiplied by its cofactor C₁ⱼ
Cofactor C₁ⱼ = (-1)^(1+j) × determinant of minor M₁ⱼ
matrixOperations.minorMatrixCofactorsDescription: Matrix obtained by removing row 1 and column {{j}}
matrixOperations.minor3x3Message: Now we have a 3×3 matrix that is easier to calculate!
matrixOperations.adjugateSquareError: The adjugate matrix can only be calculated for square matrices
matrixOperations.adjugateConceptDescription:
🎯 The adjugate (or adjoint) matrix is calculated in two steps:

1️⃣ Calculate the cofactor matrix
2️⃣ Transpose the cofactor matrix

📚 Essential for finding the inverse matrix: A⁻¹ = (1/det(A)) × adj(A)
matrixOperations.whatIsCofactorDescription:
🔍 For each element A_{i,j}, its cofactor C_{i,j} is calculated as:

• Remove row i and column j (get the "minor")
• Calculate the determinant of that minor
• Apply the sign: (-1)^{i+j}

📝 The sign pattern is like a chessboard:
matrixOperations.cofactorsCalculationDescription: We calculate some cofactors as examples:
matrixOperations.finalTranspositionDescription:
🔄 The last step is to transpose the cofactor matrix:

• Each row becomes a column
• C_{i,j} → adj(A)_{j,i}

✅ Now we have the adjugate matrix!
matrixOperations.inverseSquareError: The inverse matrix can only be calculated for square matrices
matrixOperations.whatIsInverseDescription: The inverse matrix A⁻¹ satisfies: A × A⁻¹ = I
matrixOperations.adjugateMatrixDescription: The adjugate matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix
matrixOperations.inverseMatrixFractionDescription: The inverse matrix is obtained by multiplying the adjugate matrix by {{fractionText}}
matrixOperations.resultingInverseMatrixDescription: Inverse matrix calculated with exact values
matrixOperations.rankDefinitionDescription:
The rank of a matrix is the order of the largest non-zero minor.

A "minor" is the determinant of a square submatrix.

Method: We systematically search for minors of increasing order.
matrixOperations.zeroMatrixDetectedDescription:
🔍 Examining all elements:

• All elements are zero
• No non-zero minors of any order
matrixOperations.searchingOrder1Title: 🔍 Searching for non-zero minor of order 1
matrixOperations.searchingOrder1Description:
A minor of order 1 is simply an element of the matrix.
We look for at least one non-zero element.
matrixOperations.constructingMinorsDescription:
From the base minor of order {{prevOrder}} (rows [{{rows}}], columns [{{cols}}])

We add a new row and column to form {{order}}×{{order}} submatrices.
matrixOperations.calculatingDeterminantDescription: The determinant of this {{order}}×{{order}} submatrix is:
matrixOperations.minorFoundDescription:
We found a {{order}}×{{order}} submatrix with non-zero determinant.

This means there are {{order}} linearly independent rows and columns.
matrixOperations.minorIsZeroDescription:
This particular submatrix has zero determinant.

We continue testing other combinations...
matrixOperations.maxOrderReachedDescription: We found a non-zero minor of order {{maxOrder}}, the maximum possible for a {{rows}}×{{cols}} matrix.
matrixOperations.resultForOrderDescription:
No non-zero minor of order {{order}} extending the base minor was found.

This means the rank of the matrix is {{rank}}.
matrixOperations.specialCase1x1Description: For a 1×1 matrix, the rank is 1 if the element is non-zero.
matrixOperations.fullRankMessage:
✅ The matrix has full rank (maximum possible rank: {{maxRank}}).

• All {{rows}} rows are linearly independent
• All {{cols}} columns are linearly independent
• The matrix is of full rank
matrixOperations.zeroRankMessage:
❌ The matrix is zero.

• No linearly independent rows
• No linearly independent columns
• All elements are zero
matrixOperations.partialRankMessage:
📊 The matrix has rank {{rank}} out of a maximum possible {{maxRank}}.

• There are {{rank}} linearly independent rows
• There are {{rank}} linearly independent columns
• {{dependentRows}} rows are linear combinations of others
• {{dependentCols}} columns are linear combinations of others
matrixOperations.systemCheckDescription:
System of equations: {{equations}} equations with {{unknowns}} unknowns

Matrix form: A·X = B
Where A is the coefficient matrix and B is the constants vector.
matrixOperations.augmentedMatrixDescription: We build the augmented matrix [A|B] by adding vector B as the last column:
matrixOperations.gaussianEliminationDescription: We apply Gaussian elimination to triangularize the augmented matrix:
matrixOperations.rowSwapDescription: Swap row {{row1}} with row {{row2}} to get the largest pivot.
matrixOperations.pivotNormalizationDescription: Divide row {{row}} by {{pivotValue}} to make the pivot equal 1.
matrixOperations.gaussJordanDescription: We apply full elimination to get the reduced row echelon form:
matrixOperations.homogeneousBasisVectorDescription:
Vector {{index}} of the basis of the homogeneous solution space of A·X = 0.
Corresponds to free parameter {{paramName}}.
matrixOperations.exampleGeneralSolutionDescription:
Example: X = X_p + {{paramName}}·X_1
For {{paramName}} = 1, we get a particular solution of the system.
matrixOperations.cramerVerificationDescription:
Square system: {{n}} equations with {{n}} unknowns

Cramer's rule states that each unknown xᵢ is calculated as:
xᵢ = det(Aᵢ) / det(A)
Where Aᵢ is matrix A with column i replaced by vector B.
matrixOperations.determinantStepDescription:
We calculate the determinant of the coefficient matrix A.
If det(A) = 0, the system has no unique solution and Cramer's rule is not applicable.
matrixOperations.determinantResultDescription: The determinant of matrix A is:
matrixOperations.cramerNotApplicableDescription:
Determinant of A is zero (det(A) = {{detA}}).

Cramer's rule cannot be applied because:
• The system may be incompatible
• Or may have infinite solutions

Use Gaussian elimination to analyze this case.
matrixOperations.cramerApplicableDescription:
Determinant of A is non-zero (det(A) = {{detA}}).

We can apply Cramer's rule to find the unique solution of the system.
matrixOperations.computeAiTitle: Step 2: Calculate determinants of Aᵢ matrices
matrixOperations.computeAiDescription: For each unknown xᵢ, construct matrix Aᵢ by replacing column {{i}} of A with vector B, and calculate its determinant.
matrixOperations.matrixAiDescription: Matrix A with column {{i}} replaced by vector B:
matrixOperations.detAiDescription: Calculate the determinant of matrix A{{i}}:
matrixOperations.verificationResultDescription:
Total error: {{error}}

The solution obtained with Cramer {{satisfies}} satisfies the system within numerical tolerance.
matrixOperations.formula2x2Description: We apply the formula: det = ad - bc
matrixOperations.methodSarrusDescription:
For 3×3 matrices, we apply Sarrus' Rule:
det = aei + bfg + cdh - ceg - bdi - afh
matrixOperations.resultSarrusDescription: We add the positive terms and subtract the negative ones
matrixOperations.cofactorMethodDescription:
We expand along the first row:
det(A) = a·C₁₁ + b·C₁₂ + c·C₁₃
matrixOperations.cofactorExpansionDescription: We expand along the first row of the {{n}}×{{n}} matrix
matrixOperations.cofactor3x3Description:
We expand along the first row:
det(A) = a·C₁₁ + b·C₁₂ + c·C₁₃
matrixOperations.polynomialExpansionDescription: We expand the determinant to obtain a polynomial in {{variable}}
matrixOperations.rootsCalculationDescription: We solve the equation det(A) = 0 for {{variable}}
matrixOperations.expansionStrategyDescription: We will expand along row {{row}} which has the most zeros
matrixOperations.minorCalculationDescription: Minor matrix by removing row {{row}} and column {{col}}
matrixOperations.cofactorContributionDescription: Cofactor calculation and its contribution to the determinant
matrixOperations.partialSumDescription: Accumulated sum of the terms so far
